value.body: A deck officer keeps watch on the bridge of a merchant ship, navigating it safely and overseeing cargo operations and safety equipment. Shipping companies and ship-management firms hire them for contracts at sea that often last several months. A typical day is split into watches, with navigation, cargo duties and drills in between.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc Nautical Science (3 years) or Diploma in Nautical Science (1 year), followed by sea time

items.label: Rank ladder
items.value: Deck cadet → Third Officer → Second Officer → Chief Officer → Master
items.note: Each step needs a DG Shipping Certificate of Competency

items.label: Indian seafarers (all ranks)
items.note: Officers and ratings, deck and engine combined
items.source: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways via PIB (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: After Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Maths, join a DG Shipping-approved course (entry often through IMU-CET or a sponsoring company's test) and meet the medical and eyesight standards. You then sail as a deck cadet to build sea time, and pass the Second Mate exams to get your first officer certificate.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Safety drills, firefighting and lifesaving equipment
Working in a small crew far from shore

value.title: At a glance
items: Getting a cadet berth with a company is a common hurdle after the course.
Long months at sea away from family are part of the job.
Later moves ashore include marine superintendent, port and surveyor roles.
Pay and benefits depend heavily on the company and the type of ship.
